Due to stress concentrations, scale spallation connected with internal oxidation and nitridation occurs especially at the specimen edges.

Because TiN and AlN formation is connected with a high consumption of the respective alloying elements, the coherent g8 phase (Ni3(Al, Ti, Ta)), which is responsible for the excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures, is dissolved in the near-surface region.
A deterioration of the mechanical properties of Ni-base superalloys caused by internal nitridation is expected as a result of the near-surface dissolution of the g8 phase.
This is probably due to the dendritic segregation that is typical for the solidification of single-crystalline Ni-base superalloys and is not leveled completely by heat treatment.
